message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering credible vulnerability reports and material advisory updates observed in the 24-hour window before the scheduled run on 2026-07-25 at 05:10 IST. Fresh, product-matched findings were identified for Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, and MongoDB.

**Finding 1: Google Chrome desktop security update**

- Product: Google Chrome
- Issue: CVE-2026-16804, CVE-2026-16805, CVE-2026-16806, and CVE-2026-16807
- Severity: High for all four CVEs in Google's release notes. HKCERT classifies the advisory risk as Medium Risk.
- Description: Google released Chrome 150.0.7871.186/.187 for Windows and macOS and 150.0.7871.186 for Linux with four security fixes, including use-after-free issues in Input, Blink, and WebMCP, and an out-of-bounds write in Codecs.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Google Chrome, and the advisory names Chrome desktop versions directly.
- Source: Google Chrome Releases, 2026-07-23: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/2026/07/stable-channel-update-for-desktop_01320465736.html ; HKCERT bulletin, 2026-07-24: https://www.hkcert.org/security-bulletin/google-chrome-multiple-vulnerabilities_20260724

**Finding 2: Microsoft Edge multiple vulnerabilities**

- Product: Microsoft Edge
- Issue: CVE-2026-16413 through CVE-2026-16424 as listed by HKCERT for Edge prior to 150.0.4078.96
- Severity: HKCERT classifies the advisory risk as Medium Risk. Microsoft release notes do not enumerate severity in the visible Edge page for the July 23/24 entries.
- Description: HKCERT reports multiple Edge vulnerabilities that could lead to denial of service, remote code execution, elevation of privilege, data manipulation, and security restriction bypass. Microsoft Edge release notes show Stable Channel updates on July 23 and July 24 incorporating Chromium security updates.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Microsoft Edge, and the bulletin explicitly names affected Edge versions.
- Source: HKCERT bulletin, 2026-07-24: https://www.hkcert.org/security-bulletin/microsoft-edge-multiple-vulnerabilities_20260724 ; Microsoft Edge security release notes: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-relnotes-security

**Finding 3: MongoDB multiple vulnerabilities**

- Product: MongoDB Server and MongoDB Compass
- Issue: Multiple CVEs including CVE-2026-9737, CVE-2026-13055 through CVE-2026-13078, and CVE-2026-14881
- Severity: Mixed. HKCERT classifies the overall bulletin as Medium Risk; MongoDB's own alerts include individual scores such as 9.2 for CVE-2026-13072 and 7.1 for several MongoDB Server issues.
- Description: HKCERT reports multiple MongoDB vulnerabilities affecting MongoDB Compass and MongoDB Server versions before fixed releases, with possible impacts including denial of service, information disclosure, remote code execution, security restriction bypass, elevation of privilege, and data manipulation. MongoDB's alert page confirms affected MongoDB Server version ranges and individual CVE details.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes MongoDB. The affected products explicitly include MongoDB Server and MongoDB Compass, and MongoDB-adjacent terms such as mongod/mongos were reviewed through MongoDB's security alerts.
- Source: HKCERT bulletin, 2026-07-24: https://www.hkcert.org/security-bulletin/mongodb-multiple-vulnerabilities_20260724 ; MongoDB security alerts: https://www.mongodb.com/resources/products/alerts#security

**Possible matches needing review**

- Adobe Acrobat PDF Extension for Chrome / CVE-2026-48294: Recent security coverage discussed this Adobe Acrobat extension issue, and Products.txt includes Adobe Acrobat. However, the CVE and core disclosure activity date back to June/July 22, and I could not verify a fresh vendor advisory inside this exact 24-hour window, so it is not included as a confirmed finding.
- Ubuntu snap-confine CVE-2026-8933, NGINX CVE-2026-42533, WordPress wp2shell CVEs, and 7-Zip CVE-2026-14266: These are relevant to monitored products, but the credible advisories found were published earlier than this run's 24-hour window or only surfaced as older recap coverage. They were excluded from confirmed findings to avoid reporting stale items as new.

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for browser patching because Chrome and Edge both have fresh security-update coverage, and for MongoDB deployments because the bulletin spans server-side denial-of-service, data exposure, and higher-scored MongoDB Server issues. No fresh, credible, clearly product-matched findings were verified for the remaining monitored products in this run.
